title: Super quantum groups of divided powers à la Lusztig
summary: We construct super analogues of the quantum groups of divided powers introduced by Lusztig. We call them super analogues because the Lie-theoretical data governing their structure is comparable to that of contragredient Lie superalgebras. Indeed, we show that they admit PBW-type bases parametrized by root systems of super type, and that they also have Lusztig isomorphisms giving a representation of the corresponding Weyl groupoids. Moreover, we prove that our super objects are equipped with a Frobenius-type morphism whose kernel is the Drinfeld double of a finite-dimensional Nichols algebra of super type, a super analogue of Lusztig's small quantum group, and whose cokernel is the enveloping algebra of the semisimple Lie algebra determined by the Cartan roots of the Nichols algebra. We carry out our construction within the framework of Nichols algebras of diagonal type, specifically, those whose braiding is obtained by specializing at a root of unity. This allows us to consider a divided power integral form inside a large quantum group of De Concini--Kac--Procesi type and then, via specialization, obtain our desired object.

title: Higher cluster-tilting modules for blocks of finite groups
summary: We classify the $d$-representation-finite blocks of finite group algebras over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic. The main step is to show that if a block admits a $d$-cluster-tilting module with $d\geq3$, then it splits over the fraction field of the Witt vectors. This excludes generalized quaternion defect groups of order at least $16$.

title: Harish-Chandra isomorphism over arbitrary base rings
summary: Let $G$ be a split connected reductive group scheme over $\mathbb{Z}$, and let $R$ be any commutative ring. We prove that Harish-Chandra projection induces a natural, strict filtered isomorphism $U_R(\mathfrak{g}_R)^{G_R} \simeq \operatorname{Sym}_R(\mathfrak{h}_R)^{W,\bullet}$, whereas the corresponding Chevalley restriction need not be surjective even over a field.

title: Hook histories and a two-parameter Murnaghan--Nakayama rule for dual canonical Grothendieck functions
summary: We establish a two-parameter Murnaghan--Nakayama rule for power-sum multiplication in the dual canonical stable Grothendieck basis. The coefficients admit a closed boundary product formula and a signed combinatorial description by hook histories. We determine their exact support and prove an exact divisibility law for off-diagonal coefficients governed by the edge-connected components of the indexing skew diagram. We also obtain a hook expansion of power sums, an explicit binomial reduction to the dual stable rule, and a Grassmannian $K$-homological interpretation of the one-parameter specialization. Finally, we deduce complementary rules for power-sum multiplication in the canonical basis and the corresponding lowering operation in the dual canonical basis.

title: Root-of-Unity Limits of Trigonometric qKZ Connections
summary:
Over the field of complex numbers, we study root-of-unity limits of trigonometric qKZ connections associated with tensor products of $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ Verma modules and of their hypergeometric solutions. As the multiplicative step approaches a primitive $m$-th root of unity and the quantum-group and twist parameters approach $1$, the $m$-step qKZ transport yields, on every fixed-degree subspace,a differential connection. We show that this connection is the pullback of the trigonometric KZ connection under the power map $z\mapsto z^m$, with the KZ parameter rescaled by $m$, and establish formal and $\ell$-adic versions.
  In degree one, with all highest weights equal to $1$, we determine the limits of normalized qKZ hypergeometric circle integrals in arbitrary angular chambers. The limits are expressed in terms of loaded hypergeometric integrals for the trigonometric KZ equations and explicit chamber-dependent upper-triangular matrices. We establish compatibility of the resulting distinguished fundamental matrices under inward analytic continuation, governed by the right weak Bruhat order,and under power maps, including composition of root orders.

title: Presentations of the cohomology ring of Hessenberg varieties for the minimal nilpotent orbit in type A
summary: In 2016 Abe and Crooks found a presentation for the cohomology ring of Hessenberg varieties associated with the minimal nilpotent orbit. Specifically, they presented the ring as a quotient of the cohomology ring of the flag variety, and described the kernel of the quotient map as the span of certain Schubert classes. This note improves upon their result in the Lie type A case, by giving a minimal generating set for the kernel. Our description uses substantially fewer generators than that of Abe-Crooks. Our list consists of a set of Schubert polynomials associated to permutations constructed from the Hessenberg function ${\mathbf h}$.

title: Euler up-down numbers and quiver representations
summary: We show that Euler up-down numbers enumerate isoclasses of representations arising from quiver Grassmannians which provide an explicit realization of PBW degenerate flag varieties. Using this geometric realization, we derive several formulas connecting Euler up-down numbers, median Genocchi numbers, and Motzkin numbers. We also define a new $q$-analogue of Euler up-down numbers and derive several formulas for these polynomials. We describe a natural poset structure on the set of isoclasses of subrepresentations and describe it in terms of the classical degeneration order. Finally, we prove that the finer strata defined by fixing isotypes of sub- and quotient representations are the orbits under the automorphism group of the ambient quiver representation.

title: Post-Hopf structures on $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ and post-Lie bialgebras
summary: We classify post-Hopf structures on the Drinfeld-Jimbo quantum group $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$, for $q\in\mathbb{C}^\times$ not a root of unity, proving that there are exactly three isomorphism classes. We then investigate the semiclassical limits of post-Hopf quantized universal enveloping algebras and derive a compatibility condition between the induced post-Lie product and Lie cobracket. This leads to the notion of a post-Lie bialgebra. We construct a nontrivial topological post-Hopf structure on $U_\hbar(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ and determine its semiclassical limit. For the standard Lie bialgebra structure on $\mathfrak{sl}_2$, we classify all compatible post-Lie products up to isomorphism and show that the nontrivial class admits a quantization. Finally, we formulate the general quantization problem for post-Lie bialgebras.

title: Parafermi algebra and semiprimality
comment: 11 pages; on a personal note: the present study was planned as an appendix update for [Merkel1]; due to a technical delay, it developed into a self-contained if shortish article
summary: The principles of  rational parafermi algebra of Mersenne order $p=2^n-1$, developed in an earlier work, are recapitulated in the introduction:  A Continued  Kronecker Square-root process (CKS)  dispenses with irrational numbers.The process creates two types of lower triangular square matrices, called of $G$-type and $J$-type, whose elements  decompose Catalan numbers in particular ways.  Trilinear relations, which have the lower-left matrix part interact with a suitably chosen block-diagonal part, are only semi-conservative in that  $G$-type and $J$-type elements are  preserved but appear in an operational context  showing  different direction of rotation. The second section begins with an examination of the immersion effect,  a tendency of LL$(G_{μ,ν}^{(p')})$ (for $G$-like lower-left part at order $p'\hspace*{-0.8mm}:=2^{n+1}\hspace*{-0.5mm}-\hspace*{-0.5mm}1$) to adopt  pecularities of LL$(J_{μ,ν}^{(p)})$: a semiprime  in LL$(J_{μ,ν}^{(15)})$ leads to a semiprime  in LL$(G_{μ,ν}^{(31)})$; diagonally repeated semiprimes  in LL$(J_{μ,ν}^{(31)})$ prompt diagonally repeated semiprimes in LL$(G_{μ,ν}^{(63)})$. After translating  opposing directions of rotation to differently directed paths that emerge when the ordinal number of the second factor of a semiprime with first factor 3, 7 or 11 is varied,  a rulebook is formulated which reveals that paths associated with LL$(J_{μ,ν}^{(p)})$ are not only aimed differently; they occur  five times as often as paths associated with LL$(G_{μ,ν}^{(p)})$. The coincidence of the frequency ratio ${\cal G}^{(p)}/{\cal J}^{(p)}$ with  the mass ratio of conventional matter over dark matter is commented upon at the close.

title: Coxeter Group Symmetries of Frieze Patterns
summary: Coxeter group symmetries of frieze patterns are investigated through their relation to $2\times n$ matrices and the associated Plücker coordinates. For odd order $n$, the symmetric group acts on the set of friezes, while for even $n$, the dihedral subgroup acts. We further show that a larger group acts when $n = 6$.

title: Total acyclicity of Q-shaped diagrams and N-stable categories
summary: We study total acyclicity of $\Q$-shaped diagrams of projective modules. We prove that an acyclic $\Q$-shaped diagram $P$ of projective $A$-modules is totally acyclic if and only if the associated module $K_q(P)$, or equivalently $C_q(P)$, is Gorenstein projective for every $q\in \Q$. We also establish Frobenius structures on the categories of acyclic and totally acyclic $\Q$-shaped diagrams of projective $A$-modules and introduce the associated defect category. Using adjunctions between $\Q$-shaped diagrams and chain complexes, we compare this category with the classical projective defect category and show that their vanishing is equivalent under a mild condition on the Serre functor of $\Q$. Finally, we apply our results to $N$-complexes and extend the $N$-stable equivalence of Brightbill and Miemietz beyond the Gorenstein setting, obtaining a triangle equivalence between the homotopy category of totally $N$-acyclic complexes of projective $A$-modules and the $N$-stable category of Gorenstein projective $A$-modules.

title: A proof of Casselman's comparison conjecture
summary:
We prove Casselman's comparison conjecture for parabolic subgroups of real linear reductive groups. Let $Q=LU$ be a standard parabolic subgroup of a real linear reductive group $G$, with Levi subgroup $L$ and unipotent radical $U$. For every Casselman--Wallach representation $π$ of $G$ and every $i\geq0$, the natural inclusion $π_K\hookrightarrowπ$ induces a topological $L$-equivariant isomorphism \[
  H_i(\mathfrak u,π_K)^\infty\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
  H_i(\mathfrak u,π). \] Put $\mathscr U=\mathcal U(\mathfrak u)$ and $F_k=\mathscr U/I_{\mathfrak u}^k$, where $I_{\mathfrak u}$ is the augmentation ideal. For every $k\geq1$ and $i\geq0$, we establish natural topological $L$-isomorphisms \[ \begin{aligned}
  \operatorname{Tor}_i^{\mathscr U}(F_k,π_K)^\infty
  \simeq \operatorname{Tor}_i^{\mathscr U}(F_k,π),\
  \operatorname{Ext}^i_{\mathscr U}(F_k,π_K)^\infty
  \simeq \operatorname{Ext}^i_{\mathscr U}(F_k,π). \end{aligned} \] We also obtain closedness of $\mathfrak u^kM$ for the (co)chain spaces $M=C_j(\mathfrak u,π),C^j(\mathfrak u,π)$, and for $M=J_a,J_{a-1}/J_a$, where $(J_a)$ is the smooth Bruhat filtration of a principal series representation.

title: The Partial Trace Functor on Soergel Bimodules in Type $\mathbb{B}$
summary: We write down some observations about the partial trace functor between the categories of Soergel bimodules of type $\mathbb{B}_{n+1}$ and $\mathbb{B}_n$ for future reference. In particular, we observe that, like in type $\mathbb{A}$, the partial trace sends Soergel bimodules to a semi-infinite $q$-graded sum of Soergel bimodules.

title: On the Irreducibility of Locally Analytic Vectors in Certain Banach Representations of $D^\times$
summary: We investigate the structure of locally analytic representations of $p$-adic groups, and establish a sufficient condition for the irreducibility of locally analytic vectors in certain Banach representations of $D^\times$, where $D$ is the quaternion division algebra over $\mathbb{Q}_p$. As an application, we prove that $\mathrm{JL}(ρ)^{\mathrm{an}}/\mathrm{JL}(ρ)^{1\text{-}\mathrm{alg}}$ is a topologically irreducible locally analytic representation of $D^\times$ under certain genericity conditions on $ρ$. Here $\mathrm{JL}(ρ)$ is the $ρ(-1)$-multiplicity space in the image of $Π(ρ)$ under Scholze's functor, and $Π(ρ)$ is the representation associated to $ρ$ by the $p$-adic local Langlands correspondence.

title: Exchange graphs and $τ$-tilting complexes of surface rigid algebras
comment: 42 pages, 5 figures; added results on spherical homotopy types; revised exposition and title
summary: Let $A=Λ_{\mathbf R}$ be the surface rigid algebra associated with a partial tagged triangulation $\mathbf R$ of a punctured marked surface with nonempty boundary, and let $C_A$ be the Cartan matrix of $A$. We classify the connected components of the support $τ$-tilting graph of $A$. For connected $A$, such a graph is disconnected if and only if $A$ is non-local and weakly symmetric with $\operatorname{rank}C_A=1$. The graph then has exactly two components. The completion graph of every nonzero basic $τ$-rigid pair over connected $A$ is connected. When $\mathbf R$ is nonempty and all arc endpoints are punctures, we construct an explicit homotopy equivalence from the realization of the support $τ$-tilting complex to a sphere of dimension $\operatorname{rank}C_A-1$. Under the same hypothesis, $A$ is $τ$-tilting finite if and only if $C_A$ is positive definite. In the finite case, we give a root-system realization of the $g$-vectors of indecomposable $τ$-rigid pairs, with types $A$, $D$ and $C$ determined by the tagged surface configuration.

title: An infinite completely normal basis theorem
summary: Let $L/K$ be an arbitrary Galois extension with group $G$, equipped with the Krull topology. Let $C(G,K)$ denote the $K$-vector space of continuous functions $G\to K$, with $K$ discrete and $G$ acting by left translation. We prove that there exists a $G$-equivariant $K$-linear isomorphism $\varphi:C(G,K)\to L$ such that, for every open subgroup $H$ of $G$, the map $\varphi^H:C(H,L^H)\to L$ induced by extension by zero and extension of scalars is an $H$-equivariant $L^H$-linear isomorphism. This gives a completely normal analogue of Lenstra's infinite normal basis theorem.

title: A geometric realization of socle-projective categories for posets of type $\mathbb{D}$
summary: We introduce posets of type $\mathbb{D}$, a family of posets described by an admissible Dynkin quiver of type $D_n$ together with a compatible set of extra arrows (alien arrows), and show that their socle-projective representation category is of finite representation type. Continuing, in the same spirit, a program initiated for posets of type $\mathbb{A}$ [R. Schiffler, R-J. Serna, A geometric realization of socle-projective categories for posets of type $\mathbb{A}$, J. Pure Appl. Algebra 224 (2020), no. 12, 106436], we build on an existing geometric model for cluster-tilted algebras of type $D_n$, whose geometric combinatorics is more intricate than that of type $\mathbb{A}$. Our main result establishes a $\Bbbk$-linear categorical equivalence $Θ$ between a full subcategory $(\mathcal C/T)_F$ of the arc category of a punctured $(n+3)$-gon, whose objects are certain $sp$-arcs, and the category of finitely generated socle-projective $\Bbbk\mathscr{P}$-modules, for $\mathscr{P}$ a poset of type $\mathbb{D}$. As a consequence, when the set of alien arrows is empty, we conclude that the cluster subalgebra generated by the $sp$-arcs coincides with the full cluster algebra.

title: A bar operation on the double affine Hecke algebra
summary: We construct a bar-type operation for the affine Hecke algebra $\Ha$ attached to a symmetrizable Kac--Moody group. Our main tool is a geometric bimodule defined using the equivariant $K$-theory of a suitable version of the Steinberg variety for this Kac--Moody group. Using elements of this bimodule corresponding to standard and costandard Hodge $D$-modules on the Kashiwara flag variety, we define a bar operation on $\mathcal{H}_{W}^a$ by relating the left and right actions of $\mathcal{H}_{W}^a$ on this bimodule. A central issue is that the resulting formulas for the bar operation do not preserve the algebra itself and naturally produce infinite expansions. To address this, we introduce certain completions of $\mathcal{H}_{W}^a$ on which the bar operation is well-defined. For this construction, we prove a number of combinatorial finiteness results for products in $\mathcal{H}_{W}^a$. In affine type, we further analyze the level-zero part of the algebra and obtain an explicit combinatorial formula for a bar operation on a suitable localization of Cherednik's double affine Hecke algebra. In this case the bar operation itself is not an involution but we also show that this bar operation becomes an involution when the lattice parameter $q$ is set to $1$.

title: Non-orbit 3-representation-finite symmetric algebras
comment: 5 pages. Revised title and proofs. The non-orbit argument uses a trace obstruction in place of cyclic covers
summary: We construct two $3$-representation-finite symmetric algebras over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero that are not orbit algebras of repetitive categories. This answers a question of Darpö and Iyama in the negative.

title: Feigin-Semikhatov duality at the critical level
summary:
The Feigin-Semikhatov duality asserts that the Heisenberg cosets of the subregular $W$-algebra of $\mathfrak{sl}_n$ at level $k$ and the one of the principal $W$-superalgebra of $\mathfrak{sl}_{n|1}$ at level $\ell$ coincide when the levels satisfy the Feigin-Frenkel relation $(k+n)(\ell+n-1)=1$. A similar duality holds between the subregular $W$-algebra of $\mathfrak{so}_{2n+1}$ and the principal $W$-superalgebra of $\mathfrak{osp}_{2|2n}$.
  We study these dualities in the critical/large level limit.
  We describe the centerless subregular $W$-algebra at the critical level as an orbifold of the large level limit of the principal $W$-superalgebra times a lattice VOA. Our construction yields a functor between certain categories of the two involved vertex algebras. We show that in this set-up one in fact gets block-wise equivalences of categories. Studying the principal block of the large level limit of the principal $W$-superalgebra then gives us the structure of the principal blocks of the subregular $W$-algebras in the category of weight modules (which is much larger than the more common category of lower bounded modules).

title: Jordan-Hölder property for shifted quantum affine algebras
comment: v1 and v2: 27 pages. v3: 31 pages, final version accepted in Forum of Mathematics, Sigma
summary: We prove that finite length representations of shifted quantum affine algebras in category $\mathcal{O}^{\mathrm{sh}}$ are stable by fusion product. This implies that in the topological Grothendieck ring $K_0(\mathcal{O}^{\mathrm{sh}})$ the Grothendieck group of finite length representations forms a non-topological subring. We also conjecture this subring is isomorphic to the cluster algebra discovered in arXiv:2401.04616. In the course of our proofs, we establish that any simple representation in category $\mathcal{O}^{\mathrm{sh}}$ descends to a truncation, for certain truncation parameters as conjectured in arXiv:2010.06996 in terms of Langlands dual $q$-characters.
